title: What a strings allowlist entry turns off, and what the share counts
body:
**Chose:** a `strings` entry stops every rule from reading strings in its files (`id-string`, and the string half of `line-cite` and `section-cite`); comments, names and paths there still hit. Files under an `all` entry are left out of the comment share too. An allow entry with a key other than `path` or `scope` is an error, like an unknown scope.
**Over:** turning off only the `id-string` row; counting `all` files in the share; ignoring unknown keys.
**Because:** the PRD calls the scope "the string check", and allowlisted files hold recorded tool output (`src/x.rs:3` lines, section cites) as data. Recorded fixtures under `all` are thousands of comment-free lines that would dilute the figure. A typo like `scop = "all"` would silently fall back to `strings`.
**Undo:** `scope_of` and the `strings` flag in `leaks::check`; the key check in `leaks::allowlist`.

title: The extension table and comment split beyond the PRD's list
body:
**Chose:** the js family also covers mjs, cjs, jsx, tsx, mts and cts; sh covers bash; yaml covers yml. A leading `*` makes a comment line only as `*`, `* …` or `*/`, so a Rust deref like `*count += 1` stays code. `#` starts a comment only at the line start or after a space, and `#[` in PHP is an attribute. Rust char literals, lifetimes and raw strings are parsed so a `'"'` or `r#"…"#` does not open a false string.
**Over:** the PRD's bare list and a leading `*` of any kind.
**Because:** factory's own tree has `docs.mjs`, and every false string swallows the comment behind it.
**Undo:** `leaks::syntax` and `leaks::split`.
